profile.summary: RNA-km is a language model for non-coding RNA sequences, built to predict RNA secondary structure, including pseudoknots, without training on labelled structures. It reads a single RNA sequence and returns a 1024-value representation per nucleotide and attention maps. In the paper, the attention maps are turned into base pairs with a minimum-cost flow algorithm.

summary_quotes.text: we trained RNA-km, a foundation language model that enables zero-shot prediction of RNA secondary structures including pseudoknots
extract RNA sequence representation (L * 1024) and attention maps from sequence (fasta format)
we make a zero-shot secondary structure prediction with the attention maps provided by RNA-km and a specified minimum-cost flow algorithm

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: RNA-km is a transformer encoder with 12 layers and model width 1024; the code sets the feed-forward width to four times the model width and uses relative position biases instead of absolute positions. Its token vocabulary covers A, T, C, G and X; the script converts U to T and other letters to N. It was trained by self-supervision on 23 million ncRNA sequences, using a k-mer masking strategy. A pair head projects the per-nucleotide representations to pairwise features. For structure prediction the paper uses the attention maps with a minimum-cost flow algorithm; that algorithm is not part of the repository files read.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: The repository offers one pretrained weight file, weight.pth, downloaded from Google Drive and placed in a weight folder. No version number, checksum or second checkpoint is given. A result should name the repository commit and note that the weight file comes from the Google Drive link in the README.

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: Self-supervised RNA language model (foundation model) for zero-shot RNA secondary structure prediction.

quotes.text: a foundation language model that enables zero-shot prediction of RNA secondary structures including pseudoknots

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: Transformer encoder: 12 layers, width 1024, the head count set to the width divided by 64, feed-forward width four times the model width, relative position bias (64 buckets, maximum distance 256), plus a pairwise projection of width 512.

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: One RNA sequence in FASTA format. U is converted to T and any letter other than A, C, G or T becomes N.

quotes.text: seq = "".join([_ if _ in "ACGT" else "N" for _ in seq])

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: A per-nucleotide representation of size L by 1024, saved as a .npy file; with --attn, the attention weights are saved too.

quotes.text: extract RNA sequence representation (L * 1024) and attention maps

facts.label: Parameters
facts.value: Not reported. The README, code and abstract read give no parameter count, and the weight file was not downloaded.

facts.label: Training data
facts.value: 23 million non-coding RNA (ncRNA) sequences, used without structure labels. The source database is not named in the sources read.

quotes.text: RNA-km are trained on 23 million ncRNA sequences in a self-supervised manner

facts.label: Known versions
facts.value: One pretrained weight file (weight.pth) linked from the README. No other checkpoints are described.

facts.label: Training cutoff
facts.value: Not extracted. The abstract does not date the training data and the full preprint was not read.

facts.label: Context limits
facts.value: No fixed maximum length stated. The model uses relative position biases (64 buckets, maximum distance 256) rather than a fixed-length position table.

facts.label: Weights licence
facts.value: Not stated separately. The weight file is hosted on Google Drive and the README's MIT statement refers to the repository; no licence specific to the weights is given.

facts.label: Code licence
facts.value: MIT, per the repository LICENSE (copyright 2024 gongtiansu).

strengths.text: Designed for zero-shot structure prediction: the authors use attention maps directly, without training on labelled structures, and report that they capture pseudoknots and long-distance base pairs (the authors' claim).

quotes.text: the attention maps provided by the model capture intricate structural relationships, as evidenced by accurate pseudoknot predictions and precise identification of long-distance base pairs

strengths.text: Small, readable code base under the MIT licence, with a single script that writes embeddings and attention maps to NumPy files.

quotes.text: RNA-km.py: extract RNA sequence representation (L * 1024) and attention maps from sequence (fasta format)

limitations.text: The repository only extracts embeddings and attention maps. The minimum-cost flow step that turns attention into a secondary structure is described in the paper but is not in the repository files read.

quotes.text: RNA-km.py: extract RNA sequence representation (L * 1024) and attention maps

limitations.text: The script reads only the first record of the FASTA file, taking the sequence from the second line, so multi-line or multi-sequence FASTA files are not handled.
In the script the --cuda option defaults to true, so it moves the model to a CUDA GPU even when the flag is not given.
The weights are a single file on Google Drive with no version, checksum or stated licence.

run_guide.summary: Install RNA-km at a pinned commit, place the pretrained weight file, and extract the representation of the example RNA sequence.
prerequisites: Python 3.7+ and PyTorch 1.6+, as the README states.
A CUDA GPU in practice: the script's --cuda option defaults to true. Memory needs are not stated.
A browser or other means to download weight.pth from Google Drive. Code is MIT; no weights licence is stated.

steps.title: Get the code at the pinned commit
steps.shell:
git clone https://github.com/gongtiansu/RNA-km.git
cd RNA-km
git checkout --detach 189a1cdd3bcce9d9b4d8fd612295e4d91abd21a8
steps.explanation: Clones the repository as the README says. The checkout line is added to pin the commit this page was read from.

steps.title: Install Python packages
steps.explanation: Installs the packages listed in requirements.txt. PyTorch 1.6+ must be installed separately, as the README's prerequisites say.

steps.title: Place the pretrained weights
steps.explanation: First download weight.pth by hand from the Google Drive link in the README into the repository folder; the README gives no command-line download.

steps.title: Run the example
steps.explanation: The example script runs python ../RNA-km.py -i 5E6M.fasta on the bundled sequence.

outputs: A NumPy file named after the FASTA record, holding the L by 1024 sequence representation; with --attn the file holds the representation and the attention weights.
limitations: These commands were read from the repository and have not been executed by Rewire.
The weight file must be downloaded by hand from Google Drive.
The steps give embeddings and attention maps only, not a predicted secondary structure.

notes: The repository was found by a GitHub name search; its README names the paper 'Language models enable zero-shot prediction of RNA secondary structure including pseudoknots', which matches the Europe PMC preprint by Gong and Bu (2024), so it is treated as official. Only the preprint abstract was read.
